name: two levels, left child only
code:
root = TreeNode(1)
root.left = TreeNode(2)
assert level_order(root) == [[1], [2]]

name: two levels, right child only
code:
root = TreeNode(1)
root.right = TreeNode(3)
assert level_order(root) == [[1], [3]]

name: full binary tree of height 2
code:
root = TreeNode(1)
root.left = TreeNode(2)
root.right = TreeNode(3)
assert level_order(root) == [[1], [2, 3]]

name: deeper tree, three levels
code:
root = TreeNode(1)
root.left = TreeNode(2)
root.right = TreeNode(3)
root.left.left = TreeNode(4)
root.left.right = TreeNode(5)
assert level_order(root) == [[1], [2, 3], [4, 5]]

name: skewed left tree
code:
root = TreeNode(1)
root.left = TreeNode(2)
root.left.left = TreeNode(3)
assert level_order(root) == [[1], [2], [3]]

name: skewed right tree
code:
root = TreeNode(1)
root.right = TreeNode(2)
root.right.right = TreeNode(3)
assert level_order(root) == [[1], [2], [3]]

name: tree with sparse levels
code:
root = TreeNode(1)
root.left = TreeNode(2)
root.right = TreeNode(3)
root.right.right = TreeNode(6)
assert level_order(root) == [[1], [2, 3], [6]]

name: larger tree
code:
root = TreeNode(3)
root.left = TreeNode(9)
root.right = TreeNode(20)
root.right.left = TreeNode(15)
root.right.right = TreeNode(7)
assert level_order(root) == [[3], [9, 20], [15, 7]]
